title: Galaxy Merger
intro: How do two spiral galaxies change as they pass each other? Start with a short recording, then revisit the same moment as starlight, a map of density, or individual particles.
dataset: Citizen Astronomy for Windows with OpenGL 3.3 support. The Galaxy merger scene is included with the app.
outcome: Run and replay a two-galaxy encounter, compare views of the same matter, and save a recording, a still image, or a movie.

steps.title: Open Galaxy Merger
steps.requires: Start Citizen Astronomy. If a workspace is open, choose **Mode → Choose Mode…** to return to the launcher.
actions: Scroll down to **Simulations**. Click the **Galaxy Merger** card, outlined in amber.
steps.check: The left panel says **GALAXY MERGER**. Its status says the scene is loaded. The sky view can be empty until you run the simulation.
steps.alt: The Simulations row on the CAst launcher with the Galaxy Merger card outlined.

links.label: Open a recording you already have

steps.title: Choose a starting scene
steps.requires: Open [Galaxy Merger](#launch). Save any [recording you want to keep](#save-recording) before changing scenes.
actions: Click **Simulation** (1). For this example, leave **Galaxy merger** selected. For another encounter, choose **Retrograde merger**, where one disk spins against the orbital motion, or **Seeded merger**, an alternative spiral model.
If you have a scene file instead, click **Load scene** (2), select the **.scene** file and click **Open**. A scene supplies the starting conditions for a new run.
steps.check: The selected scene name appears next to **Simulation**. The **Run** button is available.
steps.alt: The Simulation selector and Load scene button marked separately in the file controls.

steps.title: Set up a short first run
steps.requires: Select the built-in [Galaxy merger scene](#scene). Scroll to **Parameters**. Click the section heading if it is folded.
actions: Under **Resolution**, click **Minimal** (1). This reduces the number of particles CAst tracks.
Click the number beside **Steps** (2), press **Ctrl+A**, type **400** and press **Enter**.
Set **Sample every** (3) to **20** the same way. Leave **dt** at **0.005**. CAst will save a snapshot once every 20 calculation steps.
steps.check: The panel shows Minimal, 400 steps and a sampling interval of 20. This run covers 2 simulation time units, enough to practice playback while the galaxies are still separate.
steps.alt: Parameters panel with Minimal resolution, Steps at 400 and Sample every at 20 marked in order.

steps.title: Give one galaxy four spiral arms
steps.requires: Select the built-in [Galaxy merger scene](#scene). To compare with an earlier run, [save that recording](#save-recording) first.
actions: Expand **Parameters**, then click the **left** heading (1), below **Softening**. This opens the starting conditions for the galaxy named left.
Scroll to **Initial arms** (2), click its menu and choose **Four**. Leave the right galaxy unchanged so you can compare them. Scroll back up to **Run** when ready.
steps.check: The Initial arms field reads Four. The next run starts the left galaxy with that spiral pattern. Gravity can change its shape as the galaxies interact.
steps.alt: The left galaxy section is expanded, and the Initial arms selector reads Four. Both controls are outlined.

links.label: Choose a budget for the experiment

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.requires: An editable scene is loaded. For a quick first attempt, use the [400-step settings](#prepare).
actions: Scroll to the top of the left panel. Click **Run** once.
Wait until the progress bar disappears and the playback controls are available. For a long run, use the [Stop branch](#stop) to keep a partial result.
steps.check: During calculation, **Stop** replaces **Run**. Afterward, **Playback** shows a time readout and the view displays the galaxies.
steps.alt: The Run button directly below the resolution status is outlined.

steps.title: Keep part of an unfinished run
steps.requires: An encounter is currently calculating. Look for the progress bar near the top of the panel.
actions: Click **Stop**. Wait for the status to say **Stopped at step** before using the recording.
steps.check: The status gives the step reached. **Continue** appears beside **Run**. You can inspect or save the snapshots calculated so far.
steps.alt: The Stop button below an active simulation progress bar is highlighted.

steps.title: Continue a stopped calculation
steps.requires: You [stopped a run](#stop) in this session and have kept its settings.
actions: Click **Continue** beside **Run**. Keep the same parameters to preserve the stopping point.
steps.check: The progress bar returns and advances from the saved step. Choosing **Run** would start the scene over.
steps.alt: Continue is marked under the status showing the step reached when the run was stopped.

steps.title: Play, scrub and move the camera
steps.requires: Finish or stop [a run](#run), or [load a recording](#load-recording). Scroll to **Playback** and expand the heading if needed.
actions: Click **Play** (1) to move forward. Click the same button when it says **Pause** to hold a moment.
While paused, drag **Time** (2) left or right. The number above the slider is the simulated time at the selected snapshot.

Drag **Speed** (3) to the right for faster playback. To look around, left-drag in the galaxy view to orbit, right-drag to pan, and scroll to zoom. Click **Frame** beside Play to bring the encounter back into view.
steps.check: Dragging Time changes the positions shown on screen. In the 400-step example the time runs from 0 to 2. A longer encounter gives you more of the orbit to explore.
steps.alt: Real galaxy recording with Play, Time and Speed outlined next to the two galaxies.

links.label: View a disk face-on or edge-on

steps.title: Jump to the closest approach
steps.requires: Use a longer recording to see a close encounter. To reproduce this example, [select Galaxy merger](#scene), choose Minimal, set **dt** to **0.005**, **Steps** to **16000** and **Sample every** to **80**, then [run to completion](#run).
actions: Pause playback. Open **Appearance** and set **Picture** to **Optical**.
Click **First passage** (1). CAst frames the galaxies at their first close approach in the recording.
Click **After passage** (2) to advance to a later view. Use the two buttons above this tutorial screenshot to compare those actual frames.
steps.check: In this run **First passage** selects simulation time **40.8**, with the two bright centers close together. At **55.2**, the later frame shows two more widely separated centers within elongated clouds of light. A shorter recording may end before the galaxies pass.
steps.alt: Optical view at first passage with First passage and After passage outlined.

comparison.alt: The same encounter at a later time selected by After passage, with both camera buttons outlined.
comparison.label: After passage

steps.title: Turn a galaxy face-on or edge-on
steps.requires: [Pause a recording](#playback). Scroll the left panel to **Appearance** and expand the heading.
actions: Click the **Picture** selector (1) and choose **Optical** to reconstruct light from the recorded particles.
Click **Face-on disk** (2) to look down on the first disk.
Click **Edge-on disk** (3) to look along its plane. Click **Frame current light** above the two buttons to frame the emitting material again.
steps.check: The camera turns around the first galaxy, making the disk appear broader or thinner. Its playback time stays the same.
steps.alt: The optical picture of two galaxies with the Picture selector and Face-on disk and Edge-on disk buttons marked.

steps.title: Adjust starlight and dust
steps.requires: Choose the [Optical picture](#optical), pause on a frame and scroll down through **Appearance**.
actions: Drag **Exposure** (1) a short distance to the right. Watch the faint outer light as you move it.
Drag **Dust** (2) to change how strongly foreground dust absorbs starlight. Compare the same region while keeping the camera still.
steps.check: The brightness and dust contrast change on the same frame. These are illustrative brightness settings for the rendering.
steps.alt: Face-on optical reconstruction with the Exposure and Dust sliders outlined.

steps.title: Save or reuse an optical look
steps.requires: Choose [Optical](#optical) and scroll down through **Appearance** to the controls below **Stellar texture**.
actions: To keep the current settings, click **Save look** (1). Choose a folder, type a name such as **My galaxy.look**, and click **Save**.
To apply an existing look, click **Load look** (2). Select a **.look** file and click **Open**. The bundled broadband and nebular looks are examples.
steps.check: Loading a look applies its optical settings to the current scene. To keep the particle motions as well, save the recording separately.
steps.alt: The neighboring Save look and Load look buttons are each outlined.

links.label: Save a picture with this look

steps.title: Read the galaxies as a density field
steps.requires: [Pause a recording](#playback) at a time you want to inspect and expand **Appearance**.
actions: Click **Picture** (1) and choose **Illustrative volume**. Nearby particles now contribute to a continuous map of where material is concentrated.
Click **Resolution** (2) and choose **Standard** to start. This control changes the density map’s detail.
Drag **Field brightness** (3) to see fainter material. Zoom out with the mouse wheel if the map fills the frame.
steps.check: A colored volume replaces the starlight picture. The palette illustrates the distribution of material at the selected time.
steps.alt: Illustrative volume rendered from the simulation with Picture, Resolution and Field brightness marked.

steps.title: Inspect individual particles
steps.requires: [Pause a recording](#playback) and expand **Appearance**.
actions: Click **Picture** (1) and choose **Particles**.
Drag **Point scale** (2) left to shrink the points or right to make them larger. Zoom with the mouse wheel to inspect one disk.
steps.check: The smooth picture resolves into colored points. Each point represents a simulation particle. Its displayed size changes while its recorded position stays fixed.
steps.alt: Particles from a real run with Picture set to Particles and the Point scale slider outlined.

steps.title: Place stars behind the encounter
steps.requires: A [recording](#playback) is visible. Scroll down to **Background** and click its heading.
actions: Check **Stars** (1) to draw a star field behind the galaxies.
Clear **Real catalog stars** (2) to use generated stars, as shown here. To use Hipparcos positions instead, check it and click **Download star catalog** if prompted.
Move **Star brightness** (3) until the points are visible. Clear **Stars** again to remove them.
steps.check: Stars appear behind the galaxies. They are a backdrop, independent of the particles in the encounter. Saved images and video include any enabled background.
steps.alt: The Background section with Stars on, Real catalog stars off and the Star brightness slider marked.

links.label: Save the view as a PNG

steps.title: Save the simulation for later
steps.requires: You have a [finished](#run) or [stopped](#stop) calculation. Scroll to the top of the left panel.
actions: Click **Save recording**. Choose a folder and enter a name such as **First encounter.traj**. Click **Save**.
steps.check: The .traj file stores your calculated snapshots for playback. To continue calculating a stopped run, keep the current session open and use Continue.
steps.alt: Save recording is highlighted in the three-button file row.

steps.title: Reopen an existing recording
steps.requires: Open [Galaxy Merger](#launch) and locate the **.traj** file you want to view. Save any current recording you want to keep.
actions: Click **Load recording** at the top of the left panel. Select your **.traj** file and click **Open**.
steps.check: Playback becomes available with the recorded time range. To change physical parameters and calculate a different encounter, select a new scene.
steps.alt: Load recording in the top-left file row is marked.

links.label: Export the recording as a movie

steps.title: Save the current frame as a PNG
steps.requires: [Pause the recording](#playback) on the view you want to keep. Scroll to **Export** and click the section heading. Set **Format** to **PNG sequence** so Browse selects a folder.
actions: Choose a **Preset** (1), such as **1920 x 1080**, for the saved picture size.
Click **Browse** (2) and choose an output folder. Choose a fresh folder if you want to keep a previous frame.png.
Click **Save frame** (3).
steps.check: The status says **Wrote** followed by a path. Open **frame.png** there to see the camera view without the control panel.
steps.alt: Export controls with the size Preset, Browse and Save frame outlined in that order.

steps.title: Export a playable MP4 movie
steps.requires: Use a [finished or loaded recording](#playback) and your chosen camera angle. Expand **Export**.
actions: Set **Format** (1) to **MP4 (ffmpeg)**. Choose a size under **Preset** and keep **FPS** at 30 for this example.
Click **Browse** (2). Pick a folder, type **Galaxy preview.mp4** and click **Save**.
Enter a starting time in **From** (3) and an ending time in **To** (4). For the short preview, use **0** and **2**. These are times on the simulation’s playback slider.
Click **Export** (5). Wait for the export status to report completion, then open the MP4 in a video player.
steps.check: The frame count and target filename appear below the time range. At 30 frames per simulation time unit, a range from 0 to 2 produces 60 frames.
steps.alt: Movie settings with MP4 Format, Browse, From, To and Export outlined.

steps.title: Export a numbered PNG sequence
steps.requires: A [recording](#playback) is available. Expand **Export**. Choose your image size under **Preset**.
actions: Set **Format** (1) to **PNG sequence**.
Click **Browse** (2) and select a folder for the images. Set **From** and **To** to the part of the recording you want to keep.
Click **Export** (3). If you stop a sequence early, leave its settings in place and click **Continue** in the Export section to finish it.
steps.check: The selected folder fills with numbered PNG images, one per exported frame. Each uses the chosen camera and appearance.
steps.alt: Export panel highlighting PNG sequence format, the output folder chooser, and Export.
